title: Bounds-check motion_visualization composite bbox rendering to eliminate IndexError on 16:9 frames
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-14, post alert-quality review)
plan_section: V2-024 follow-up (composite rendering) + V2-031 follow-up (single-bbox padded crops rounded mult32)
trigger: Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim): 'OK, so, my Car, me, and my dog have all been active around the building and have many alerts. Overall, they look very good ... Now none of them matched any known vehicle vehicles, or people or animals, so we probably want to look at that aspect of it, but let me know overall how things are going in your opinion.' Alert review on logs/daemon.log (2026-09-11 through 2026-09-14, 1817 /alert POSTs) found 227 HTTP 500 crashes (12.5% of alerts) caused by IndexError in infra/motion_visualization.py:378. Of 4 alerts sampled from the operator's reported car/human/dog activity, 3 returned 500 silently: the operator was getting real alerts but ~1 in 8 were silently dropped without Telegram delivery.
background: Traceback (from logs/daemon.log, alert_id=a7101065-b971-4b8a-b3c7-fc7fefcef967 and ~225 others): File '.../infra/motion_visualization.py', line 378, in _draw_rectangle arr[y1 - dy, x0:x1 + 1] = green IndexError: index 1296 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 1296. Root cause: _native_bbox_to_corners (lines 113-131) clamps y1 against min(W - 1, ...) instead of min(H - 1, ...). On 1920x1080 frames (W=1920, H=1080), y1 gets clamped to 1919 instead of 1079, then _draw_rectangle writes past arr.shape[0]=1080. Secondary issue: _draw_rectangle does not bounds-check y0-dy or y1+dy against arr height, nor x0-dx/x1+dx against arr width; any unclamped or edge-case bbox can IndexError. V2-024 PRD acceptance specified render_motion_composite works on the refactor's test fixtures (which used square or near-square bboxes), so the bug never surfaced. V2-031 added rounded-mult32 padding to crops; that change multiplied the number of edge-case bboxes hitting the buggy clamp. fix is mechanical: (1) clamp y1 against H not W; (2) clamp all four (y0,y1,x0,x1) inside _draw_rectangle as defense in depth.

shipping_definition: (a) _native_bbox_to_corners clamps y1 against H-1 (not W-1). (b) _draw_rectangle clamps all four edges against arr.shape before writing. (c) New edge-case test in tests/test_motion_visualization.py covers a 1920x1080-frame bbox where y0+h > H_orig (the production failure mode). (d) `python -c 'import infra.motion_visualization'` exits 0. (e) `pytest tests/test_motion_visualization.py` passes including the new edge-case test. (f) Full pytest still green. (g) commit on main with US-040 in the message. Working tree clean.

design_principles: Minimal surface change. Two files: infra/motion_visualization.py (clamp fixes) + tests/test_motion_visualization.py (new edge-case test).
_native_bbox_to_corners is a pure helper — clamp against the CORRECT dimension (H for y, W for x).
_draw_rectangle is defense in depth — clamp all four edges against arr.shape regardless of caller (future-proofing).
Edge-case test reproduces production failure: 1920x1080 frame, bbox with y0+h > H_orig so the old code would IndexError.
Single commit on main with US-040 in the message.
Re-run daemon's existing /alert path is the integration verification (operator does this manually post-merge).

stories.notes: Reproducer for the production bug: alert_id a7101065-b971-4b8a-b3c7-fc7fefcef967, BACK camera, crop_bbox_b=(454, 848, 704, 448). Native frame 1920x1080, y0=848, h=448, so unclamped y1=1296; with the old code, y1 was clamped to min(W-1=1295, 1296)=1295, then arr[y1-dy, ...] crashed because arr.shape[0]=1296 in this case but the IndexError on production was arr.shape[0]=1080 (real 16:9 frames). Fix AC2/AC3 verify the y1-clamp against H. AC4 is the integration test that reproduces the IndexError with a 1920x1080 frame and asserts render succeeds. _draw_rectangle defense-in-depth clamps all four edges against arr.shape so future callers can't reproduce the IndexError either.
